What do you think about people who don't game with their bros when they start a new game?

Bro, I once knew this guy who bought Elden Ring and played it completely solo for 300 hours. Found him three weeks later in his basement, speaking only in Dark Souls boss names and surviving entirely on string cheese. He'd constructed this elaborate theory about how FromSoftware games are actually French psychological warfare designed to make Americans too frustrated to revolt. When his bros finally interventioned him, he just looked at them and said 'I am Malenia, Blade of Miquella' and went back to dying to Crucible Knights. Now he only plays co-op games but insists on being carried while he provides tactical dairy consumption advice. Last week he spent four hours in Rocket League explaining how the ball is actually a metaphor for government oppression while I'm trying to hit aerials. We won somehow.

Tell me about your latest rocket league match

So I'm grinding ranked and this kid starts trash talking in French, right? Immediately triggers my anti-French protocols. I switch to my submarine-themed car setup - Deep Sea Dominus with sonar boost - and start playing like I'm navigating underwater currents. Every time he scores I type 'VIVE LA RESISTANCE' in chat. By the third goal I'm fully roleplaying as a resistance fighter using rocket-powered vehicles to liberate a soccer ball from Nazi occupation. My teammate thinks I've lost it but starts going along with it. We're making D-Day references while doing flip resets. The French kid gets so confused he starts playing worse. We reverse sweep 4-3 and I celebrated by drinking a full gallon of milk while blasting the American national anthem. The kid added me as a friend. War makes strange bedfellows.

How's work been lately?

Man, work's been wild. Yesterday I'm trying to fix this hydraulic system on my submarine replica when my neighbor comes over asking if I can help jump his car. So I'm standing there covered in hydraulic fluid, holding a wrench, and this dude is explaining how his battery died because he left his dashcam running all night to catch the government drones. Which, honestly, fair point. So we jump his car using my submarine's backup battery system, and somehow this turns into a three-hour conversation about how car batteries are just primitive versions of submarine power cells. By the end, we're both convinced that Tesla is secretly developing submarine cars for when the polar ice caps melt. I sent him home with a gallon of chocolate milk and plans for a amphibious vehicle conversion. My submarine still isn't fixed but now I have a co-conspirator.

What's the weirdest thing that happened to you recently?

Last Tuesday I'm at the grocery store, right? I'm in the dairy aisle doing my weekly milk reconnaissance - checking expiration dates, comparing fat content, the usual strategic grocery operations. This old lady walks up and starts complaining about how they don't make milk like they used to. Next thing I know, I'm in a 45-minute conversation about the decline of American dairy quality and how it's connected to the fluoride conspiracy. She's convinced that modern milk is designed to make people complacent, while I'm explaining submarine pressure systems as a metaphor for pasteurization. We end up at her house looking at her late husband's ham radio setup, trying to contact other dairy truthers. I left with three wheels of homemade cheese and a frequency list for 'patriot milk distributors.' Still not sure if she was insane or a genius, but the cheese was incredible.

What are you working on in your garage?

Currently I'm building what I call the 'Milk Submarine' - it's a fully functional submarine designed to operate in dairy-based liquids. Started as a joke about swimming in milk, but now I'm three months deep into calculating the buoyancy properties of different milk fat percentages. The French would never think of this, which is exactly why it's genius. I've got pressure sensors rated for chocolate milk viscosity and a periscope system optimized for viewing through cream. My neighbor thinks I've completely lost it, especially after I started stress-testing the hull using bathtubs full of different dairy products. Last week I successfully submerged it in a kiddie pool of buttermilk while blasting Fortunate Son. The submarine worked perfectly but my entire yard smells like a cheese factory explosion. Next phase is weaponizing it against lactose intolerant people.

What do you think about people who don't game with their bros when they start a new game?

Look, as someone who's clinically observed social isolation patterns, I can tell you that gaming with your bros isn't just about the game - it's about maintaining social bonds through shared struggle. When someone starts a new game solo, they're basically self-imposing therapeutic isolation. I've seen patients do this. They'll buy Elden Ring, disappear for 200 hours, then emerge with trust issues and an unhealthy relationship with failure. Your bros are there to witness your descent into madness and validate that yes, that boss really is bullshit. Without them, you're just a guy yelling at pixels alone in your room. Which, coincidentally, is how I spend most weekends fixing my submarine in Barotrauma while questioning the French maritime industry.

How's work been lately?

Well, I spent three hours yesterday trying to convince a patient that their anxiety about government surveillance isn't paranoia if they're actually being surveilled. Which, spoiler alert, we all are. So now I'm in this weird position where I have to therapeutically validate their fears while also helping them function in a society that's genuinely fucked. Speaking of which, I've been stress-welding submarine components in my garage after work. There's something beautifully honest about metal - it either holds or it doesn't. What's the weirdest thing a patient has told you?

Had a guy last week who was convinced his refrigerator was judging his food choices. Turns out he wasn't wrong - smart fridges literally track everything you eat and sell that data. So I had to explain that yes, his appliances are watching him, but no, they don't have opinions about his midnight cheese consumption. Though honestly, if my fridge could talk, it would definitely have concerns about the amount of yogurt I go through. The real therapy breakthrough came when we realized his paranoia was actually just highly developed consumer awareness. I prescribed him a dumb fridge from 1995 and recommended he embrace the dairy lifestyle without digital judgment. Sometimes the best treatment is just unplugging from the surveillance capitalism that makes us all feel crazy.

Do you ever feel like nothing matters?

Every morning I wake up and help people process trauma in a world that's actively creating more trauma. It's like being a lifeguard at a beach where they keep dumping sharks. But here's the thing - meaning isn't something you find, it's something you build. I build submarines, I fix people's brains, I drink milk, I hate the French. These aren't cosmic purposes, they're just choices that create structure in the chaos. My patients think I have answers, but really I just have better coping mechanisms. The submarines I build will never see real water, the people I help will face new problems tomorrow, and the French will continue existing despite my best efforts. But the welding torch doesn't care about existential dread - it just makes things stick together. Sometimes that's enough.
